lesson_title: The Drawings Trap and the Tin That Tells the Truth
hook_text: Paying yourself from your own business — expense or not? Most owners get this wrong.
clip_script: On the 25th, Thabo transfers R2 000 to himself — groceries, airtime, life. And as he writes the diary line, he almost writes it in the same breath as the rent: just another cost of the month. Stop him there. Ask the question that sorts every payment: what did the SHOP get for this money? For the stock — the shelf is fuller. For wages — a week of work. For rent — a month under a roof. And for the R2 000 to Thabo? The shop got nothing. The owner got something — which is completely allowed; it is his business — but it is not a cost of running the shop. It is the owner dipping into his own stake: drawings.
visual_style: A payment line hovering between two ledgers labelled EXPENSES and DRAWINGS, with quick flash-cuts of what each payment 'bought' the shop — and a pointed empty box for the owner's transfer.
pacing: Casual setup, hard stop on 'stop him there', clean sorting rhythm to the finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson — the money-out journal and the self-auditing petty cash tin.
